package.title: How slowing AI development could make it more useful.
package.promised: Slower, more deliberate AI development may produce systems that are much more reliable at completing multi-step tasks. I expect to see an illustrative comparison showing why higher per-step reliability dramatically improves the odds of an entire job being finished correctly.

new_things: Slower development could make AI useful faster.
More reliable steps could let the same AI finish more jobs.
Anthropic’s boss called for pacing frontier AI development rather than stopping training.
reports.held_question: How can higher reliability in individual steps make an AI complete more whole jobs?

new_things: A twenty-step job with steps that each work 95% of the time finishes without any mistake only 36% of the time, if failures are independent.
Raising each step’s reliability from 95% to 99% increases clean completion.
reports.held_question: How much more often does the whole job finish cleanly when each step works 99% of the time?
reports.asked_of_me: Imagine a job with twenty steps, each working 95% of the time.
